failure_reason: Direct HTTP (curl_cffi) and headless Playwright were blocked by Akamai on every /shop/ path; headed Playwright (real Chrome, non-headless) reached the main New Arrivals PLP successfully before also hitting a 403 on a later page. Escalated to Claude-in-Chrome (last-resort tier; robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow), a browser instance shared across 10 concurrent workers on this task -- after verifying the main listing, its tab-group/session assignment became unstable (rapid, uncontrollable reassignment to different tab groups between consecutive tool calls, including several 'Chrome extension disconnected' errors), which prevented opening any further pages for the remainder of this pass. Only the single comprehensive 'All New Arrivals' listing could be fully verified as a result; the site's own per-department New Arrivals sub-listings (see notes) were identified as likely genuine but never opened, so per the brief's 'a candidate is only valid once you open it' rule they are reported as unconfirmed candidates in notes rather than as rows.
notes: Access route as in the other two files for this company. Navigation discovery: homepage header nav has a 'New' link (/shop/new/). Opening /shop/new/ itself shows it is a category-hub/landing page (links out to sub-pages, no product grid or item-count control of its own, generic H1) -- correctly excluded as not itself a PLP, matching the brief's Collection-page test. Its child /shop/new/all-new/ IS a genuine PLP: real product grid with prices and 'NEW' badges, breadcrumb/H1 'New Arrivals', and a 'View 620 Items' count control -- included below. That all-new page's own on-page nav pills additionally list per-department tabs: Dorm, Furniture, Bedding, Study, Backpacks & Lunch, Decor, Lighting, Lounge, Window, Rugs, Bath/Pajamas & Robes, Harry Potter, Halloween -- and the site's own shop-sitemap-index.xml (fetched directly via curl_cffi) additionally lists /shop/new/new-furniture/, new-bedding/, new-study/, new-decor/, new-lighting/, new-lounge-seating/, new-storage/, new-backpacks-luggage/, new-rugs/, new-windows/, new-bath/, new-get-ready/, new-beach/, and all-new-christmas/ following the exact same '/shop/new/new-<dept>/' URL family as the confirmed all-new/ page. This is a strong signal of genuine per-department New Arrivals sub-structure (directly parallel to the verified Best Sellers and Clearance per-department pages for this same company), but none of these department URLs were actually opened before the tooling became unusable, so none are reported as rows -- they should be re-checked in a follow-up pass. Separately, the sitemap also lists several other /shop/new/* URLs (accessible-collection-old/, no-kid-hungry-shop/, st-jude-shop/, jordan-chiles-old/, kenzo-lee-old/, fair-trade-shop/, secret-all-products/) whose naming (charity-partnership shops, athlete-collab shops, '-old' suffixes, a 'secret-' prefix) indicates they are very likely NOT New Arrivals listings but themed/legacy pages nested under the same URL prefix; these were not opened either and are excluded rather than guessed at.

rows.evidence: Breadcrumb/H1 'New Arrivals', 'View 620 Items' product-count control on the page
